remediation.title: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Asha’s team is building a model bridge together. What is the best way for the team to work?
questions.options: Everyone shares ideas and takes turns to talk | The tallest person makes all the decisions | The fastest person builds it alone | Each person hides their ideas from the others
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone shares ideas and takes turns to talk
questions.explanation: A good team lets everyone share ideas and take a turn. That way the bridge gets the best thinking from the whole team.

questions.question: Omar is sharing his idea with the team. What should the rest of the team do?
questions.options: Talk over him with louder ideas | Walk away and start building | Cover their ears until he stops | Look at him and listen until he has finished
questions.correctAnswer: Look at him and listen until he has finished
questions.explanation: Good teammates listen with their eyes and ears until the speaker has finished. Then everyone can talk about the idea together.

questions.question: Asha’s team gives everyone a job: drawer, builder, counter and speaker. How does this help the team?
questions.options: It stops the team from talking to each other | It lets one person rest while the others work | Everyone knows their part, so the work is shared fairly | It makes the work take longer on purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone knows their part, so the work is shared fairly
questions.explanation: When each person has a job, everyone helps and nobody is left out. Sharing the work fairly is what strong teams do.

questions.question: Asha asks every teammate the same question and makes a tally mark for each answer. What is she doing?
questions.options: Guessing what her team thinks | Carrying out a little survey to collect answers | Drawing a picture of her team | Playing a counting game with no purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Carrying out a little survey to collect answers
questions.explanation: Asking everyone the same question and marking each answer is a survey. The tally marks keep her count safe so she can check it later.

questions.question: In a playground game, only the tallest children are allowed a turn. What is the fairest thing to say about this rule?
questions.options: It is not fair, because games should have no rules at all | It is fair, because rules are always right | It is fair, because tall children are older | It is not fair, because everyone should get a turn
questions.correctAnswer: It is not fair, because everyone should get a turn
questions.explanation: A fair rule treats everyone the same. Being tall does not decide who deserves a turn, so this rule leaves people out unfairly.

questions.question: Bilal is being a rule detective. He asks, ‘Why do we walk, not run, in the corridor?’ What is the most likely reason for this rule?
questions.options: Walking makes the corridor longer | Teachers do not like children moving | The rule has no reason at all | Running indoors can knock people over and hurt them
questions.correctAnswer: Running indoors can knock people over and hurt them
questions.explanation: Rules usually have a reason behind them. Walking keeps everyone safe in a busy corridor — that is the reason a rule detective finds.

questions.question: Zahra’s class wants one new classroom rule. Which rule is the best choice?
questions.options: We take turns and share the equipment | Nobody may ever ask a question | The first child to arrive owns the classroom | Only Zahra’s friends may use the crayons
questions.correctAnswer: We take turns and share the equipment
questions.explanation: A good rule keeps things safe and fair for everyone, not just for a few. Taking turns and sharing treats every child the same.

questions.question: Bilal wants to find out more about the library rule. Which question would help him learn the most?
questions.options: Why do we have this rule in the library? | What colour is the library door? | Is the library open today? | Do you like books?
questions.correctAnswer: Why do we have this rule in the library?
questions.explanation: A ‘why’ question opens up the reason behind the rule. The other questions get short answers that do not explain anything.

questions.question: Layla is going to talk with her grandmother about life long ago. What should she do before the visit?
questions.options: Plan to read a book during the visit | Wait and hope questions appear by themselves | Decide all the answers before she asks | Think of good questions and write them down
questions.correctAnswer: Think of good questions and write them down
questions.explanation: Researchers get ready before they ask. Writing her questions down means Layla will not forget them when the visit starts.

questions.question: Layla wants her grandmother to tell her more about the old days. Which question is best?
questions.options: Are you very old? | Can I go and play now? | Did you play games? | What games did you play when you were young?
questions.correctAnswer: What games did you play when you were young?
questions.explanation: An open question invites a whole story, not just ‘yes’ or ‘no’. ‘What games did you play?’ lets Grandmother share much more.

questions.question: After the visit, Layla thinks: ‘I used to believe life long ago was boring — now I know it was full of games.’ Why is this kind of thinking useful?
questions.options: It helps her forget the visit quickly | It shows her how her ideas changed after learning something new | It proves she was right all along | It means she never has to ask questions again
questions.correctAnswer: It shows her how her ideas changed after learning something new
questions.explanation: Looking back at what you used to think and what you know now is reflection. It shows Layla that learning changed her mind.

questions.question: Which of these is a need, not just a want?
questions.options: A bag of sweets | A new video game | Clean water to drink | A gold bracelet
questions.correctAnswer: Clean water to drink
questions.explanation: A need is something we must have to live and stay healthy, like clean water. Toys, sweets and jewellery are wants — nice, but not needed.

questions.question: A banana travels from the farm, to a lorry, to a ship, and then to the shop. Who does the very first job in the banana’s journey?
questions.options: The captain who sails the ship | The farmer who grows the bananas | The shopkeeper who sells the bananas | The customer who eats the banana
questions.correctAnswer: The farmer who grows the bananas
questions.explanation: Every food journey starts with growing. The farmer’s work comes first, before the lorry, the ship and the shop.

questions.question: Two friends suggest different snacks for the class. Amina gives a reason: ‘Fruit keeps us healthy.’ Faduma only says: ‘Because I like it.’ Whose idea is stronger, and why?
questions.options: Amina’s, because she gives a reason everyone can think about | Faduma’s, because liking something is always right | Neither, because ideas never need reasons | Both the same, because they are friends
questions.correctAnswer: Amina’s, because she gives a reason everyone can think about
questions.explanation: An idea with a clear reason is easier to judge and trust. Amina explains why her idea helps everyone, so hers is stronger.

questions.question: Hassan learned about fairness at school. Which of these shows he is using what he learned at home?
questions.options: He always chooses the game because he is older | He lets his sister do all the tidying alone | He hides the toys so nobody can play | He takes turns with his sister when choosing the game
questions.correctAnswer: He takes turns with his sister when choosing the game
questions.explanation: Reflection means taking what you learn and using it in your own life. Taking turns at home shows Hassan really understood fairness.

questions.question: A new pupil joins the class and stands alone at break time. How might the new pupil be feeling?
questions.options: Bored of her many friends | Angry that the school exists | Sure that everyone already knows her | Shy and a little lonely
questions.correctAnswer: Shy and a little lonely
questions.explanation: Imagining how someone else feels helps us know how to help. A new pupil with no friends yet often feels shy and lonely.

questions.question: What is the best way to help the new pupil feel welcome?
questions.options: Learn her name and invite her to join your game | Only talk to her if the teacher says so | Wait for her to make friends by herself | Tell her the class is already full
questions.correctAnswer: Learn her name and invite her to join your game
questions.explanation: Welcoming someone means taking the first kind step. Learning her name and inviting her in helps her feel part of the class.

questions.question: Sami wants to greet a new neighbour who speaks a different language. What can he do?
questions.options: Smile, wave and say hello slowly and kindly | Stay silent because words are impossible | Speak very fast so it is over quickly | Turn away so he does not make a mistake
questions.correctAnswer: Smile, wave and say hello slowly and kindly
questions.explanation: A smile and a friendly wave are understood in every language. Speaking slowly and kindly helps his hello travel across languages.

questions.question: Maryam wants to find out where the rice in her kitchen comes from. Which of these would help her most?
questions.options: Guessing a country she likes | Asking her baby brother | Reading the label on the rice packet | Drawing a picture of rice
questions.correctAnswer: Reading the label on the rice packet
questions.explanation: The label is a source of information — it often tells you where food was grown or packed. Reading it beats guessing every time.

questions.question: A food label says: ‘Grown in Somalia. Packed in Egypt.’ Where was the food grown?
questions.options: The shop | The label does not say | Egypt | Somalia
questions.correctAnswer: Somalia
questions.explanation: Read the label carefully: ‘grown in’ tells you where the food came from first — Somalia. Egypt is only where it was packed.

questions.question: Warsame is counting the bottles he finds on the beach. Why is it a good idea to make a tally mark for each bottle?
questions.options: The tally keeps an exact count he can check later | The tally makes the number of bottles smaller | The marks look pretty in his notebook | He can change the tally to any number he likes
questions.correctAnswer: The tally keeps an exact count he can check later
questions.explanation: A tally records every bottle as he finds it, so the count stays exact. Trying to remember big numbers is easy to get wrong.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What happens if we waste things?

questions.question: Warsame wants to learn how to recycle plastic. Which source will help him most?
questions.options: A friend’s guess | A poster about a football match | A library book about recycling | A cartoon about pirates
questions.correctAnswer: A library book about recycling
questions.explanation: A helpful source talks about your question. The recycling book is about recycling — the cartoon, the poster and a guess are not.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What happens if we waste things?

questions.question: Bilal wants to know which game his classmates like best. What is the best way to find out?
questions.options: Choose his own favourite for everyone | Ask every classmate and write down their answers | Wait quietly and hope somebody tells him | Ask only his best friend
questions.correctAnswer: Ask every classmate and write down their answers
questions.explanation: To find out what a whole class thinks, ask the whole class. Writing the answers down means none of them get lost.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: How can we be active and healthy?

questions.question: Bilal’s survey shows that most children chose football. What is a clear way to share what he found with the class?
questions.options: Keep the results secret in his bag | Show the counts and say which answer got the most votes | Say that lots of things happened and sit down | Read out every child’s name very fast
questions.correctAnswer: Show the counts and say which answer got the most votes
questions.explanation: Sharing findings clearly means showing the numbers and saying what they tell us. Then everyone understands what the survey found.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: How can we be active and healthy?

questions.question: Ayan reads Yusuf’s letter about moving to a new town. What is the best way for her to understand how he felt?
questions.options: Decide that letters are always made up | Imagine how she would feel in his place | Skip the feelings and count the words | Think only about her own town
questions.correctAnswer: Imagine how she would feel in his place
questions.explanation: Putting yourself in someone else’s shoes is how we understand their feelings. Ayan imagines his move as if it were hers.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What is it like to move here?

questions.question: Nura’s grandmother teaches her a song from long ago. What is a kind thing for Nura to say?
questions.options: Please stop singing now | Thank you for teaching me | I already know everything | Songs are boring
questions.correctAnswer: Thank you for teaching me
questions.explanation: Saying thank you shows we value what someone shares with us. It is a small sentence that makes people feel appreciated.

questions.question: Hodan must choose which of two gardens she likes best. What should she do?
questions.options: Say she cannot ever choose anything | Let someone else decide for her | Look carefully at both gardens, then choose and say why | Choose one without looking at them
questions.correctAnswer: Look carefully at both gardens, then choose and say why
questions.explanation: Choosing well means looking first, then picking and giving your reason. Saying why you like something makes your choice strong.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Adam wants to know what a nurse does at work. What is the best way to find out?
questions.options: Ask a nurse about their job | Guess and never check his guess | Look at pictures of a completely different job | Ask a friend who does not know either
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a nurse about their job
questions.explanation: The best person to tell you about a job is someone who does it. Asking a real nurse gives Adam true answers.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Which of these wastes water?
questions.options: Using a small cup of water to rinse | Leaving the tap running while brushing your teeth | Turning the tap off after washing your hands | Fixing a dripping tap
questions.correctAnswer: Leaving the tap running while brushing your teeth
questions.explanation: Water that runs down the drain while nobody uses it is wasted. Turning the tap off keeps that precious water safe.

questions.question: The class is making a big food display together, and every child has a part to add. What makes the display turn out well?
questions.options: The children hide their parts from each other | Everyone waits for someone else to start | Each child does their part and helps the others | One child does everything alone at night
questions.correctAnswer: Each child does their part and helps the others
questions.explanation: When everyone adds their part and helps each other, the whole display comes together. Working together makes big jobs possible.
